pr_title: Bluetooth: ISO: Add support for cis_established_v2 in host
pr_body:
Add support for the bt_hci_evt_le_cis_established_v2 event in the host.

This provided additional information to the host and application about the CIS paramters. Especially the peripheral gets new an important information such as the SDU size and interval.

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/79554

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: ISO: Add support for CIS established event V2
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Bluetooth Core 6.0 added a new version of the `HCI_LE_CIS_Established` event which adds additional information to the CIS peripheral when a CIS is connected, such as the `Sub_Interval`, `Max_SDU_C_To_P`, `Max_SDU_P_To_C`, `SDU_Interval_C_To_P`, `SDU_Interval_P_To_C`, and `Framing`. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an vent handler for the version 2 of the event similar to 
```c
	EVENT_HANDLER(BT_HCI_EVT_LE_CIS_ESTABLISHED, hci_le_cis_established,
		      sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_le_cis_established)),
```

The version 2 can likely be handled similar to the version 2 of `BT_HCI_EVT_LE_PER_ADVERTISING_REPORT_V2`. 

The additional new informaton should be stored in `store_cis_info`. 

The TX in the ISO shell for the peripheral also needs to be updated to use the new value (if available): https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/bluetooth/host/shell/iso.c#L487-L495

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
Since this is not supported by all ISO controllers, we need to ensure that they support the event. See also https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/79555

review_comments: I'm wondering if we should rather set it to a value which makes it clear that the SDU size is unknown

Had the same thought. In the current version of Zephyr we do fallback to the PDU size, as that is the only value the CIS peripheral has. Setting it to an "UNKNOWN" value may prevent CIS peripherals from sending anything if they use the `sdu` field here, rather than the `pdu` field of the `info` struct

But I'm OK with either approach
I would prefer setting it to to 0 when unknown. The app developer can use `can_send` and `can_recv` to detect if the SDU size is actually non-zero

Since this would be unrelated to supporting this event, and require changes to tests and samples that use the qos.sdu value, I suggest that if we modify it, we do it in a separate PR, and keep existing functionality for this value

Would it be better to set it to an invalid value in this case? 

Went with this approach, as that was the previous approach when setting the tx->sdu and rx->sdu for peripherals.
Should we guard the event and all fields from the event with a Kconfig option?
I would keep it unguarded to avoid adding to many Kconfig options
